claims.text: All compared alloys have homogeneous, single-phase FCC microstructures after consistent thermomechanical processing.
APT and HAADF-STEM can be used to map and quantify atomic-scale lattice distortions and chemical inhomogeneities in these alloys.
Local lattice distortions arise from atomic-size and elastic-modulus mismatches among the constituent elements.
The quinary Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy has more intense local lattice distortions than its equiatomic quaternary and ternary FCC subsets.
Additional elemental interactions in the quinary alloy intensify local lattice distortions.
Local lattice distortions produce fluctuating internal stress fields.
The fluctuating internal stress fields hinder dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation glide increases yield stress and flow stress.
Impeded dislocation glide alters strain localization and work-hardening behavior.
Relative to the quinary baseline, the quaternary alloys should exhibit less pronounced local lattice distortions.
Relative to the quinary baseline, the ternary alloys should exhibit less pronounced local lattice distortions.
Relative to the quinary baseline, the quaternary and ternary alloys should have lower yield strengths.
Relative to the quinary baseline, the quaternary and ternary alloys should have lower flow stresses.
Relative to the quinary baseline, the quaternary and ternary alloys should have diminished work-hardening rates.
The magnitude of local lattice distortion should correlate with yield strength, flow stress, strain localization, and work-hardening behavior.
A lack of significant differences in lattice-distortion magnitude among the alloys, or a lack of correlation between distortion and mechanical performance, would falsify the proposed mechanism.
